rows.grounds: describes the world as lacking permanence
abstract state of being fixed or permanent
proper name meaning the fixed one

items.question: How can Dhruva attain fixedness while perceiving this unfixed world?
premises: This world is observed as not fixed.
Dhruva is the one who sees this world.
Attaining fixedness is questioned despite perceiving impermanence.
items.inference: The apparent fixedness of Dhruva stands in tension with the unfixed nature of the world he perceives.
items.plain_english: Seeing this unfixed world, did that Dhruva not attain fixedness?

rows.grounds: those who go to desired abodes
refers to the goddess or power

items.question: What power does the goddess hold to delight even the seven sages journeying to desired abodes?
premises: The seven sages travel to desired abodes.
Even these sages experience delight through meeting her.
Her presence causes delight in those who seek higher realms.
items.inference: The goddess possesses a delight-giving power that affects even accomplished sages.
items.plain_english: Even the seven sages, going to their desired abodes, are delighted by meeting her.

rows.grounds: her whose body is consciousness itself

items.question: How is the consciousness-embodied goddess made ever newly apprehensible on the path within the body?
premises: The path is situated within the body.
She is embodied as consciousness itself.
She is caused to be grasped ever anew.
items.inference: On the embodied path, the goddess of consciousness-nature reveals herself in ever-fresh apprehensions.
items.plain_english: On the path within the body, they cause one to grasp her, whose form is consciousness itself, ever new, ever new, ever new.

rows.grounds: through acts of seeing or revelations
visions of this world and the other world attained

items.question: By what visions does the mind become filled with experiences of this world and the beyond?
premises: The mind is filled through visions.
These visions include this world and the other world.
Such visions are attained experiences.
items.inference: The mind becomes enriched by visions encompassing both worldly and transcendent realms.
items.plain_english: With the mind, one fills oneself through visions, by visions of this world and the other world that have been attained.

items.question: Why does the guru praise the goddess as the teacher of the three worlds?
premises: The guru establishes reverence among gurus.
The guru praises her.
She is identified as the guru of the three worlds.
items.inference: The goddess is extolled as the supreme teacher whose authority encompasses all three worlds.
items.plain_english: The guru, establishing weight among gurus, praises her as the guru, the teacher of the three worlds.

rows.grounds: in whom all auspiciousness has arisen
all-auspicious through union with Śiva's body

items.question: What makes the goddess the object of worship as the source of all auspiciousness?
premises: She is worshipped.
All auspiciousness has arisen in her.
Her auspiciousness is united with Śiva.
items.inference: The goddess is worshipped because she embodies complete auspiciousness in union with Śiva.
uncertainties: Compound segmentation of aṅga+lagna+śiva+sarva+maṅgalām follows traditional reading but internal relations are compact.
items.plain_english: One worships her, in whom all auspiciousness has arisen, who is all-auspicious through union with Śiva.

items.question: How is the goddess duly worshipped with radiant offerings at her feet?
premises: Heaps of jewels shine at her feet.
These jewels illuminate like a shining crown.
She is duly worshipped with such radiance.
items.inference: Worship of the goddess is expressed through luminous, jewel-like offerings at her feet.
items.plain_english: Illuminating her feet with heaps of jewels shining like a crown, one duly worships her.

rows.grounds: one whose mind is attached to the supreme power

items.question: What enables the poet to celebrate the goddess with unrestrained inspiration?
premises: The poet has taken refuge in her.
His mind is attached to the supreme power.
He poetizes her without restraint.
items.inference: Attachment to the supreme power frees the poet to celebrate the goddess unrestrainedly.
items.plain_english: Having taken refuge in her, the poet whose mind is attached to the supreme power poetizes her unrestrainedly.

items.question: Why does the wise person fully worship the awakened sovereign goddess through firm determination?
premises: The wise person acts through determination.
The goddess is awakened and possesses sovereignty.
He worships her fully.
items.inference: Decisive understanding leads the wise to fully worship the awakened, sovereign goddess.
uncertainties: The token īśvaritām+āṃ is treated as a fused form indicating possession of sovereignty.
items.plain_english: Therefore, O gentle one, the wise person, through determination, fully worships her who is awakened and possesses sovereignty.

items.question: How is the noble, playful goddess worshipped as the sovereign lord with blossomed lotuses?
premises: The worshipper acts himself.
He offers blossomed blue lotuses.
He worships her as the lord displaying noble play.
items.inference: The goddess is worshipped as sovereign through offerings of blossomed lotuses that honor her noble play.
items.plain_english: He himself worships this lordly goddess of noble play with blossomed blue lotuses.

items.question: Why does even the heavenly sun contemplate the goddess whose light pervades all?
premises: Even the sun of heaven is described as contemplating her.
Her light is pervading.
The sun's own radiance is subordinate in this contemplation.
items.inference: The goddess's all-pervading light surpasses even the heavenly sun, making her the object of its contemplation.
uncertainties: The image puccha+mūrcchitaḥ is unusual and may carry a specific symbolic sense.
items.plain_english: Even the sun of heaven, with raised tail, here contemplates her whose light is all-pervading.

items.question: What qualities of the goddess are recalled through subtle contemplation of her power?
premises: She subdued the anger of Daksha.
She is skilled in wisdom or awakening.
She is remembered with a subtle mind.
items.inference: Subtle contemplation recalls the goddess as both subduer of destructive anger and bestower of wisdom.
items.plain_english: With a subtle mind, one remembers her who subdued Daksha's anger and who is skilled in awakening.

rows.grounds: beings associated with the elephants of the sky
as chief of the fragrant or divine world

items.question: Why do the sky-elephant beings bow to the goddess under her title as chief of the divine world?
premises: Sky-elephant beings bow to her.
They address her by a specific name.
That name identifies her as chief of the divine world.
items.inference: Her sovereignty over the divine realm elicits homage from celestial beings.
uncertainties: The exact identity of antarikṣa+gaja+nāḥ is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: The beings of the sky-elephants bow to her by the name 'chief of the divine world'.

rows.grounds: with multitudes of their own wings
her who possesses sovereignty over sky-dwellers

items.question: How do celestial beings honor the goddess who holds sovereignty over sky-dwellers?
premises: They fan her with multitudes of their own wings.
Their wings serve as fine chowries.
She possesses sovereignty over sky-dwellers.
items.inference: The goddess's sovereignty over sky-dwellers is honored by their own wings serving as ceremonial fans.
items.plain_english: They fan her, who possesses sovereignty over the sky-dwellers, with multitudes of their own wings as fine chowries.

items.question: How can the same goddess be worshipped everywhere as each devotee's chosen deity?
premises: Devotees bow to her in various places.
She assumes distinct forms.
Each worships her as their own chosen deity.
items.inference: The goddess manifests in distinct forms so that she can be the chosen deity of devotees in different places.
items.plain_english: In various places, they bow to her, who assumes distinct forms, as their own chosen deity.

rows.grounds: whose object remains beyond all remainders

items.question: How do unblinking seers praise the goddess who transcends all remaining objects?
premises: Unblinking seers praise her.
They use various epithets.
Her objecthood transcends all remainders.
items.inference: Even transcendent reality is praised through epithets by seers of unblinking vision.
uncertainties: The compound śeṣa+śeṣa+viṣayāṃ is interpretively dense.
items.plain_english: Those with unblinking vision praise her, whose object transcends all remainders, with various epithets.

rows.grounds: with recitation, fire offering, and libation

items.question: What ritual practices prescribed in many tantras are used to worship the goddess?
premises: Worship is performed with recitation, oblation, and libation.
These practices are prescribed in many tantras.
They are beneficial and extensively performed.
items.inference: Tantric ritual worship of the goddess consists of extensive, beneficial practices of recitation, oblation, and libation.
items.plain_english: They worship her with recitation, oblation, and libation, prescribed in many tantras, beneficial and extensively performed.

rows.grounds: through the lineage of the guru

items.question: What role does the guru's lineage play in the swift arising of joy within the practitioner?
premises: Something was clearly and quickly accomplished through the guru's lineage.
Joy entered the speaker.
The speaker became filled with that joy.
items.inference: Transmission through the guru's lineage brings about the swift and clear entry of joy into the practitioner.
items.plain_english: Clearly and quickly accomplished through the guru's tradition, joy indeed entered me and came to abide in me.

items.question: What realization grants the speaker the power to create, remove, or transform all reality?
premises: By a certain power the speaker becomes capable.
This capability includes doing, removing, and transforming.
The scope of this capability is all this.
items.inference: The realized power enables the speaker to create, withdraw, and transform the entirety of reality.
items.plain_english: Ah, by which I am capable of creating, removing, or otherwise transforming all this!

rows.grounds: among the most massive or gross

items.question: How can the realized principle be both subtler than breath and the giver of all desires?
premises: It is lighter than breath.
It is very firm among the greatest.
It grants all desired desires.
items.inference: The realized principle unites supreme subtlety, supreme stability, and the power to fulfill all desires.
items.plain_english: Lighter even than breath, very firm among the greatest, and the giver of all desired desires.

rows.grounds: by the nature of being the self of all

items.question: How does manifesting all as one's own self reveal the source of arising and dissolution?
premises: Being is manifested as the self of all.
This existence is identified as such.
It is the source of both arising and non-existence.
items.inference: Realizing all being as one's own self reveals the principle that is the origin and dissolution of existence.
items.plain_english: Manifesting being through the nature of being the self of all, this existence is the source of arising and dissolution.

items.question: How did the facing of the two principles give rise to the moving and unmoving world?
premises: Two principles are present.
Their facing toward manifestation opens.
The moving and unmoving world is fashioned from this.
items.inference: The interaction of the two principles in manifestation produces the entire moving and unmoving world.
uncertainties: The identity of the two principles (etayoḥ) depends on the immediate context.
items.plain_english: Through the opened facing of these two, I fashioned the various moving and unmoving world.

rows.grounds: named as the triad enclosing all
the state of letters, words, and sentences

items.question: How does the triadic enclosing line give rise to the levels of linguistic expression?
premises: A line is named as the triad enclosing all.
From this arises the state of letters, words, and sentences.
Linguistic levels emerge sequentially.
items.inference: The all-enclosing triadic principle unfolds into the structured levels of language from letter to sentence.
uncertainties: The specific referent of rekhayā and the triad is technical and context-dependent.
items.plain_english: Then, by the line named the triad enclosing all, there arose the state of letters, words, and sentences.

rows.grounds: philosophical views or systems of seeing
by the nature in which seen and seeing are dissolved
the creation or emanation of sound

items.question: How does the dissolution of seer and seen relate to the creation of philosophical visions and sound?
premises: The nature of seen and seeing is dissolved.
Philosophical visions arise.
The emanation of sound is created by the speaker.
items.inference: From the dissolution of subject-object duality, the speaker creates both the emanation of sound and the various systems of vision.
items.plain_english: Thus, by the dissolution of the nature of seen and seeing, the various visions and the creation of sound were fashioned by me.
